title: The quotient normalization is the scalar-adjunction composition mate
statement: Let T be a scheme and d an adic coefficient datum. For a ≤ b, let π_b and π_a be the completed coefficient projections and q the quotient map from level b to a, so π_b q = π_a. The conjugate, under the published derived scalar adjunctions for π_a and the composite of those for π_b and q, of the published normalization completedReductionDerivedNormalization T d b a h is the inverse of pbcDerivedRestrictComp π_b q π_a. The normalization is the one fixed by the balancing formula on K-flat representatives, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism. This uses the actual coefficient maps and derived scalar adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower].

source.place: lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; mates composition and adjoint uniqueness. The stated equation specializes these constructions to the published coefficient maps. Also literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex and Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Mates.lean.

proof.text: Use the normalized ordinary scalar adjunctions. The transpose of the ordinary balancing map, followed by the identity-on-sections restriction compositor, sends x to 1 tensor x, by evaluating the two units and the balancing map on tensor generators. Thus it is the ordinary unit for the composite coefficient map.

The derived Hom comparison and its cochain compatibility identify transposes of universal scalar counits on every representative. Compose these formulas with normalizedAdjunction_composition and use exactDerivedRestrictionComposition_inv_factors for the right comparisons. The normalized adjoint-uniqueness theorem then gives precisely the two-counit balancing formula for the left-adjoint uniqueness map.

Uniqueness in completedReductionDerivedNormalization_exists identifies this comparison with the published normalization. The left-adjoint composition isomorphism is the inverse of the conjugate equivalence applied to the inverse restriction compositor, so applying conjugateEquiv gives the assertion. Equal levels and the zero coefficient quotient require no cancellation of elements and are included.

lean.statement:
theorem completedReductionNormalization_scalarMate
    (T : Scheme.{u}) {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A]
    (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (b a : ℕ) (h : a ≤ b) :
    conjugateEquiv (pbcDerivedScalarAdjunction (d.projection T a))
        ((pbcDerivedScalarAdjunction (d.projection T b)).comp
          (pbcDerivedScalarAdjunction (reductionCoefficientMap T d b a h)))
        (completedReductionDerivedNormalization T d b a h) =
      (pbcDerivedRestrictComp (d.projection T b) (reductionCoefficientMap T d b a h)
        (d.projection T a) (completedReductionProjection_comp T d b a h)).inv
